binders: Implicit positive-candidate parameters K and rho and a packaged system with pressure p and velocity u.
Arbitrary real x,t and proposed values ptt,pxx,uxt,utx for second or mixed derivatives.
hypotheses: The system packages first partial derivatives satisfying p_t+K*u_x=0 and u_t+(1/rho)*p_x=0 at every point.
ptt is the t-derivative at t of the function τ -> p_t(x,τ), where p_t is computed by deriv.
uxt is the t-derivative at t of τ -> u_x(x,τ).
utx is the x-derivative at x of ξ -> u_t(ξ,t).
pxx is the x-derivative at x of ξ -> p_x(ξ,t).
mathematical_definitions: p_t,p_x,u_t,u_x are defined using the total derivative operator deriv with the other coordinate fixed.
The four HasDerivAt hypotheses identify the relevant second and mixed partial values.
c=sqrt(K/rho) is the principal nonnegative real square root and c^2 is ordinary natural-number squaring.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every positive real K and rho and every packaged solution (p,u) of the first-order acoustics system, at any point where p_tt, p_xx, u_xt, and u_tx exist in the explicitly stated iterated-derivative sense and the mixed velocity derivatives commute (u_xt=u_tx), pressure satisfies the wave equation p_tt=c^2 p_xx with c=sqrt(K/rho).

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The conclusion is conditional on explicit existence of four iterated derivatives and equality of the two mixed velocity derivatives; no theorem that these hypotheses follow from a broader smoothness class is included.

The derivative operator deriv is totalized, but the surrounding HasDerivAt hypotheses identify genuine derivatives of the first-partial functions; the packaged system supplies genuine first partials at every point.
Only the pressure wave equation is concluded, not the analogous velocity wave equation.
The statement is pointwise over all real x,t and contains no initial/boundary conditions, global solution representation, uniqueness, or energy claim.
Although c^2 equals K/rho under positivity, the conclusion is written using (sqrt(K/rho))^2 rather than simplifying the coefficient.
The implication is vacuous at choices of ptt,pxx,uxt,utx that do not satisfy the derivative hypotheses; when the hypotheses hold, derivative uniqueness fixes these values.
